results.name: Basílica de la Sagrada Família
results.why_it_is_special: Antoni Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece and UNESCO World Heritage Site; an extraordinary fusion of Gothic and Art Nouveau forms inspired by nature, geometry, and spirituality — one of nine UNESCO sites in the city.

results.name: Park Güell
results.why_it_is_special: A Gaudí-designed public park and UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring mosaic-covered structures, organic forms, and panoramic views over the city.

results.name: Casa Batlló
results.why_it_is_special: Remodelled by Gaudí between 1904 and 1906 for textile industrialist Josep Batlló; its undulating façade, skeletal balconies, and dragon-scale roof make it one of the most imaginative buildings in European modernism.

results.name: Casa Milà (La Pedrera)
results.why_it_is_special: Gaudí's last civil work before dedicating himself to the Sagrada Família; a UNESCO-listed apartment building with a sculptural stone façade and a rooftop of surreal chimneys.

results.name: Museu Picasso
results.why_it_is_special: Housed in five medieval palaces, it holds one of the most extensive collections of Pablo Picasso's early works, offering deep insight into the artist's formative years in Barcelona.

results.name: Fundació Joan Miró
results.why_it_is_special: Opened in 1975 in a light-filled building in Parc de Montjuïc, the foundation houses over 14,000 pieces by Joan Miró and hosts rotating temporary exhibitions — an intimate, curated experience overlooking the city.

results.name: MACBA (Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona)
results.why_it_is_special: A striking white geometric building designed by Richard Meier; it showcases thought‑provoking contemporary art from the late 20th century to the present and anchors El Raval's creative scene.

results.name: MNAC (Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya)
results.why_it_is_special: Occupying the Palau Nacional, it spans a thousand years of Catalan art — from Romanesque church murals to modernisme — making it the most comprehensive survey of regional art anywhere.

results.name: Mercat de la Boqueria
results.why_it_is_special: Barcelona's oldest and most famous food market, dating back to the 13th century; a sensory explosion of fresh produce, seafood, and local specialties that captures the city's deep relationship with food culture.

results.name: Mercat de Santa Caterina
results.locality_or_neighbourhood: Ciutat Vella (Sant Pere, Santa Caterina i la Ribera)
results.why_it_is_special: Built in 1845 on the site of a former convent, it features a spectacular undulating mosaic roof by Enric Miralles and Benedetta Tagliabue — a less touristy alternative to La Boqueria with excellent local produce.

results.name: Mercat dels Encants (Fira de Bellcaire)
results.why_it_is_special: One of Europe's oldest flea markets and a treasure trove for vintage lovers, now housed under a striking mirrored canopy — a Barcelona off-the-beaten-path favourite.

results.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
results.locality_or_neighbourhood: Ciutat Vella (Sant Pere, Santa Caterina i la Ribera)
results.why_it_is_special: A UNESCO World Heritage concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner in the Catalan modernista style; its stained‑glass skylight and ornate interior make it one of the most beautiful music venues in the world.

results.name: Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau
results.why_it_is_special: Designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner, this former hospital is a breathtaking Modernist complex and UNESCO World Heritage Site, now repurposed as a cultural centre and knowledge hub.

results.name: El Born Centre de Cultura i Memòria
results.why_it_is_special: A 19th-century iron-and-glass market hall converted into a cultural centre after a €84 million renovation; beneath its floor lie archaeological remains of 18th-century Barcelona, making it both a museum and a monument to the city's memory.

results.name: CaixaForum Barcelona
results.why_it_is_special: A former Modernist textile factory converted into a dynamic arts centre hosting world‑class travelling exhibitions, film cycles, and educational programmes — a top attraction on Barcelona's official tourism list.
